'''C. Paul Robinson''' (October 9, 1941 – March 2, 2023) was an American [[physicist]].<ref>{{Cite web |url=http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?robinsonc |title=C. Paul Robinson &#124; Array of Contemporary American Physicists |access-date=2015-04-03 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20150408015650/http://www.aip.org/history/acap/biographies/bio.jsp?robinsonc |archive-date=2015-04-08 |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name=obit />

== Biography ==
Robinson was born in [[Detroit, Michigan]] on October 9, 1941.<ref name=obit>{{cite news|url=https://www.sandia.gov/labnews/issue/remembering-paul-robinson/|work=Sandia LabNews|title=Remembering Paul Robinson|date=March 6, 2023|author=Rebecca Ullrich}}</ref> He received his Ph.D. in physics from [[Florida State University]] and spent most of his career at [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] and [[Sandia National Laboratories]], becoming President of Sandia Corporation in 1995.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.sandia.gov/about/history/index.html|title = Sandia National Laboratories: About Sandia: History}}</ref>  He served as head of delegation and chief negotiator for the United States in the Nuclear Testing Talks with the [[Union of Soviet Socialist Republics]].<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://2001-2009.state.gov/t/isn/isab/75675.htm|title = Amb. C. Paul Robinson}}</ref>  These negotiations produced Protocols to the [[Threshold Test Ban Treaty]] and the [[Peaceful Nuclear Explosions Treaty]]. Both, along with the treaties, were ratified unanimously by the [[U.S. Senate]] and remain in force. The negotiations included agreement for, and execution of, the [[Joint Verification Experiment]], carried out in 1988 as the Kearsarge event in [[Operation Touchstone]]. He died on March 2, 2023, at the age of 81.<ref name=obit />

==Awards and honors==
* Member, [[National Academy of Engineering]], Special fields and interdisciplinary (1998)
* [[George E. Pake Prize]] (2003)
